PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve rebound backends during provisional cleanup (#343…
PullRequest.Body:
…104)

* agentHost: preserve rebound backends during provisional cleanup

Track backend ownership after draft graduation so workspace changes and UI cleanup cannot replace or delete a running conversation. Keep rebound lookups stable and reject rebinding a non-owned source.

Fixes #342665



* agentHost: ignore folder changes for disposed provisional entries

Capture the entry once and skip folder re-picks for disposed or non-owning entries, matching the surrounding lifecycle guards.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each workspace-folder change fanned out over all tracked sessions; every rebound session whose desired roots changed could schedule one agent-host createSession and one disposal of its previous backend.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Workspace changes could cause avoidable per-started-session host I/O, provider initialization, and teardown latency.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added ownership guard skips rebound, non-owning entries during workspace-root reconciliation, preventing their backend recreation and disposal while preserving the existing behavior for owned untitled drafts.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, the workspace-folder listener skipped only disposed entries, so rebound started sessions reached _reconcileWorkspaceRootSet. A changed root set then reached _reconcileGeneration, which calls IAgentHostService.createSession and disposes the prior generation across the agent-host protocol. Node-side creation initializes a provider and touches database/filesystem state; disposal performs database, provider, and storage cleanup. Added tests verify that workspace-folder changes now produce zero create and disposal calls for rebound sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Graduate an untitled provisional draft into a started/rebound conversation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: tryRebind is serialized behind prior draft work. A reusable generation requires one confirmed agent-host dispatch; otherwise one agent-host createSession must finish before the new mapping is published. The ownership flag assignment is local and adds no boundary work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Confirm the final config against a reusable backend session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one confirmed dispatch for one graduation when a matching generation exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same confirmed dispatch occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before rebind can publish the real-resource mapping.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a backend session when the provisional generation cannot be reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful create per cold graduation, with retry only when concurrent config/folder state invalidates a candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create path and retry checks existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation must complete before graduation can publish the new mapping.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose a temporary provisional generation when graduation created a distinct backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one normal post-publication disposal per graduation, plus pre-existing stale-candidate retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same temporary-generation disposal occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the mapping is published but before tryRebind resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source draft per call; aggregate work scales with simultaneously graduating drafts, with per-source serialization and no changed global limiter.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SequencerByKey serializes operations for the source session. Separate drafts can graduate concurrently; the diff does not change that concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A matching in-memory generation is the warm state and avoids createSession; a missing/mismatched generation takes the cold create path. There is no changed negative cache. Marking the published rebound entry non-owning preserves that generation rather than invalidating it on later workspace events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full rebind control flow and each host call are explicit, and the diff only marks ownership after successful creation/reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup and remote-host latency vary, but the diff adds no graduation boundary or multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The first graduation retains existing boundary behavior, while a later attempt to rebind the non-owned result now exits before host work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change workspace folders, selected folder, or agent root capabilities while drafts and started conversations are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event callback scans tracked entries synchronously, then queues reconciliation asynchronously per affected owned draft. Stable owned generations avoid host work; mismatched owned drafts create a replacement and dispose the old backend. Rebound entries are now skipped, so their conversations make progress without reconciliation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a replacement provisional backend with the new working-directory set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for warm matching generations; otherwise one successful create per affected owned draft, with stale-candidate retries only under concurrent state changes. After the diff, zero for rebound entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same event also reached rebound entries, producing one create for each affected started session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the synchronous event callback, but required before the draft exposes a stable replacement generation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Kind: IPC/network cleanup with host database/filesystem/provider work
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose the previous backend after publishing its replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per successfully replaced owned draft generation; zero for rebound entries after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, affected rebound sessions also disposed their prior running backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before reconciliation resolves, though the replacement is published first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve session config after recreating an owned draft at a newly selected folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per successful selected-folder change for an owned draft; zero for rebound entries after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Folder events could invoke this for rebound mappings before the new ownership guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the queued folder-change operation completes, after backend replacement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The synchronous scan is O(number of tracked mappings). Expensive work scales with owned drafts whose desired roots actually differ; effective cardinality excludes all started/rebound sessions after this diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session operations are serialized by SequencerByKey. Multiple owned drafts can reconcile concurrently across keys; this pre-existing burst is reduced because all rebound entries are excluded.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The published generation plus desired working directories form a positive cache: unchanged state returns immediately. Owned drafts invalidate by state mismatch. Non-owning rebound entries now always retain their published generation for this service. No miss retry or negative-cache behavior is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership guards are present at every event entry point and generation matching, and new tests assert zero creates/disposals for rebound sessions across folder additions, removals, and selection changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The typical number of simultaneously open drafts and frequency of workspace changes are unknown; provider create/dispose cost varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff fixes a concrete boundary fan-out by removing per-rebound-session create/dispose/config-resolution work and does not increase work for owned drafts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose a chat model, provisional mapping, or the provisional service
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Entry maps and lifetime bindings are released synchronously. Owned abandoned drafts queue or fire-and-forget one agent-host disposal; rebound mappings perform local cleanup only because the started backend is no longer owned by this provisional service.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Kind: IPC/network cleanup with host database/filesystem/provider work
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per disposed owned entry that has a generation; zero per rebound/non-owning mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, explicit or event-driven cleanup also deleted the backend behind a rebound started session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by explicit disposeSession callers; chat-model event callers fire it without awaiting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fire-and-forget backend disposal during service shutdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per owned generated draft plus pending cleanup entries; rebound entries are excluded after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, shutdown also requested disposal for each tracked rebound backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the synchronous shutdown critical path because promises are not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Local cleanup scales with tracked entries; host disposal scales only with owned draft generations after the diff, not all rebound conversations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: disposeSession is serialized per resource. Service shutdown can issue disposals concurrently across owned drafts, as before, but the diff removes rebound sessions from that burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cleanup cache. _removeEntry deletes all local maps and disposes the entry lifetime. Pending failed backend disposals retain existing retry-on-host-start behavior only for owned cleanup attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownsBackend is set false exactly when the real mapping is published, and every changed cleanup branch checks it; tests cover chat-model, mapping, and service disposal for both ownership states.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of abandoned drafts at shutdown is unknown, but changed cardinality is strictly lower and rebound entry lifetimes are still locally disposed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change transfers backend cleanup responsibility away from this provisional service after graduation while still releasing its local entry, bindings, and maps.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold. The ownership state and guards reduce agent-host create/dispose/config calls for rebound sessions, preserve per-key sequencing, and do not add unbounded retention or new critical-path work. Recorded the removed workspace-change fan-out as a concrete regression fix tied to its introducing commit.
